Verified closed on candidate sha256:f55095dbec364594d25a624261512239854f233d3ee0b5c8ecc210d1602bf6e0 (757 files, recomputed in a complete clone at the freeze commit d22938f; source d3e6fe6). The repair is T-DG3-KBE-I (1cd89e6, merged in e210987). The product diff c40232b0..d3e6fe62 is exactly fuzz.test.ts, the ADR-0024 section 6 'Pinned by tests' sentence and the p3-work-split amendment 29. eslint.config.js and every engine source are unchanged (diff-scan.log D1-D5).

1. Re-run of my round-6 check of the test.
- independent-row-lint.mjs is my own linter, run outside the candidate's test. It takes the 101 PROBES rows from a runtime dump made in a separate disposable copy, and lints each with ESLint as packages/shared/src/formula/tokenize.ts.
- Result: 99 rows are refused by a formula-block guard rule. The two 'unbalanced' rows (`const s = "unclosed;` and `function f() {`) are fatal parse errors. No row is unguarded.
- In round 6 the test linted 48 of 99 rows and accepted any rule. It now lints 99 of 101, requires a guard rule, and pins the count (linted === PROBES.length - LINT_EXCLUDED.size). A separate test pins the exclusion list.

2. Mutations M1 and M2, in a disposable clone (lint-mutation-probe.mjs, Node 22.22.2).
- Control: the candidate test is green.
- M1 (removes `ForOfStatement[await=true]`): exit 1. The failing assertion is 'for await (const x of xs) a(x); (await): expected [] to not deeply equal []'.
- M2 (removes the `PrivateIdentifier[...]` part): exit 1. The `class C { #then() {} }` row fails.
- The same two mutations against the PRE-REPAIR test (c40232b0) both survive (exit 0). So the repair is what closes the round-6 gap.
- The clone's git status is '' afterwards.

3. The section 6 sentence is exactly true. Each element checked against the code and the evidence:
- 'lints with ESLint.lintText as if they were formula/tokenize.ts': yes.
- 'G1, G2, A1, A2 and F1 helpers (each must be refused by its named rule)': yes. ROUND5_HANDLER_FORMS gives no-restricted-syntax for each form; F1_FORMS gives no-unsafe-finally.
- 'every row of the probe table except the two unbalanced rows, which must instead be parse errors': yes, 101 rows, 99 linted and 2 fatal.
- The seven guard rules listed are exactly the formula block's own rules (eslint.config.js no-eval .. no-unsafe-finally). A parse error or a general rule does not count: the filter is `r !== null && GUARD_RULES.has(r)`.
- p3-work-split amendment 29 ('99 of 101', the two private-name rows, M1/M2) is also exact.

Observation, not a finding. My informational ablation (lint-mutation-probe ABL-*, lint-ablation-2, lint-ablation-full) removed each selector part of the formula block in turn and ran the whole fuzz.test.ts.
- Every L1-L7 form stays pinned by some test.
- The only L-part pinned by no test is the computed `["then"]` member part. That part is redundant: the pinned `Literal[value=then]` part still refuses `p["then"]`.
- Several layer-1 constructor/timer/require/computed-key parts are pinned by no unit-node test. The 'Pinned by tests' bullet sits inside the L1-L7 list and makes no claim about them. The source scan (layer 2) and the no-codegen run (layer 3) cover those forms (the 18 round-2 forms are still 'BLOCKED BY BOTH').
- So no sentence is false, and there is no behavioural gap.

4. F-DG3-100 does not regress. All five F-DG3-100 probes were re-run VERBATIM; their sha256 values are in probes-summary.txt:
- G1 G2 G3 E1 E2 H1 H2 S1 S2;
- A1 A2 F1 F2 H3 H4;
- W1-W6;
- S1-S3 V1 V2;
- the 18 round-2 forms.
Every verdict line is byte-identical to round 6 (probe-verdicts-r6-vs-r7.log). The spellings (53/53 refused by lint) and the residual A3/A4 are also identical to round 6.
